question.worked_solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

This question requires the product rule. Let $u(x)={x}^{4}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡(3x-1).$ Then

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=4{x}^{3},\,{v}^{′}(x)=-3\operatorname{csc}⁡(3x-1)\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x-1).
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the product rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(4{x}^{3})(\operatorname{csc}⁡(3x-1))+({x}^{4})(-3\operatorname{csc}⁡(3x-1)\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x-1)) \\  & =4{x}^{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(3x-1)-3{x}^{4}\operatorname{csc}⁡(3x-1)\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x-1) \\  & ={x}^{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(3x-1)(4-3x\operatorname{cot}⁡(3x-1)).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x})|}_{x=1} & =(1)^{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(3(1)-1)(4-3(1)\operatorname{cot}⁡(3(1)-1)) \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡2(4-3\operatorname{cot}⁡2).\end{aligned}
$$
